key_insight: DualG-MRAG separates global multi-hop reasoning from fine-grained evidence matching by using two graphs, reducing noise while preserving local visual and textual details.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a practical design pattern for building more accurate multimodal retrieval-augmented generation systems on complex, multi-hop queries.
method: Build a Macro Graph for global topological routing across heterogeneous documents and modalities.
Build a Micro Graph for precise local verification of fine-grained evidence.
Use a GNN Retriever for query-driven message passing and dynamic-programming decoding to extract reasoning paths for generation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive experiments showing improvements in both evidence recall and complex QA accuracy over baselines.
watch_item: The dual-graph and dynamic path-extraction pipeline may add implementation complexity and higher compute/memory costs in large multimodal retrieval settings.
paper_title: DualG-MRAG: Decoupling Macro-Reasoning and Micro-Matching for Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
